card.keepWhy: Every time you come back, that’s one more rep.
sources: Bhagavad Gita 6.34 (Arjuna: the mind is restless, turbulent, strong and stubborn; holding it is as hard as holding the wind)
Bhagavad Gita 6.35 (Krishna: no doubt the mind is restless and hard to hold, but it is held by abhyasa, practice, and vairagya, dispassion)
check: vairagya glossed as “letting go” (more exactly dispassion, non-attachment); confirm this is fine for beginners.

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? how busy is your mind right now? you try to focus, and end up somewhere else.
options: then you’re in good company. listen.
then this one will help. listen.
lovely. listen anyway, it’s a good one.

steps.line: In the Gita, Arjuna says what everyone thinks: Krishna, the mind is restless, stubborn, and strong.
Controlling it is like trying to control the wind.

steps.q: Arjuna isn’t a monk on a mountain. Who is he, and where is this talk happening?
o: A student, in a forest school
A warrior prince, before a battle
A king, holding court in his palace
steps.why: The whole Gita is a talk in a chariot between two armies at Kurukshetra. Arjuna asks about his restless mind with a war about to start.

steps.q: Arjuna says the mind is impossible to control. What do you think Krishna says?
steps.why: He agrees. Then he gives two words. Watch.

steps.line: Krishna doesn’t argue. You’re right, he says. It’s hard.
Then he gives two words. Abhyasa: practice. And vairagya: letting go.
steps.label: abhyasa

steps.q: Vairagya is often translated “letting go.” Letting go of what?
o: Of having any feelings at all
Of grabbing at what pulls you off
Of home, to live as a monk
steps.why: Not numbness, and not running away. Vairagya is loosening your grip on cravings, so the mind has less to chase.

steps.line: You train the mind the way you train anything: by coming back to it, again and again.

steps.q: Why does Krishna agree with Arjuna first, before giving any advice?
o: The mind can’t really be trained
It was the quickest way to end it
Honesty first makes the advice land
steps.why: Krishna doesn’t pretend it’s easy. A restless mind isn’t a failure. It’s where the practice starts.

steps.line: Your mind isn’t broken. It’s untrained. Every time you come back, that’s one more rep.
steps.label: today

say: here’s what i love. krishna doesn’t tell arjuna to stop thinking. he says, you’re right, it’s hard.
in the gita, the mind is trained by abhyasa, practice, and vairagya, letting go. you don’t win in one sitting. you come back, again and again.

steps.q: You sit for two minutes and your mind wanders ten times. Each time, you come back. In Krishna’s words, what just happened?
o: It only counts if it never wanders
steps.why: Every return is one rep of abhyasa. The wandering isn’t the failure. Coming back is the practice.

today.say: set a two-minute timer. watch your breath. each time your mind wanders, smile and come back. that’s abhyasa. some hindus sit with a mantra, like “om,” instead of the breath. you can try either. it’s your choice.
options: good. count the comebacks, not the wanderings.
so was arjuna’s. that’s exactly who krishna answered.
